summary: Lane County, OR summit in the Umpqua NF: 40-ft L-4 tower 1933, replaced by a 41-ft R-6 tower (1955 or 1962, sources differ); tower moved to Cinnamon Butte in 1976.

facts.design: 1933: 40-foot round fir pole tower with 14x14 L-4 cab; replacement 41-foot treated timber tower with R-6 cab
facts.status_note: No tower stands at the Buster Butte summit; the R-6 tower was moved to Cinnamon Butte in 1976 and stands there

visit.trail_note: No tower stands at the Buster Butte summit. A 1962 News-Review item describes a logging road built for the timber sale

events.note: Register: a crow's nest and shelter set up on the site in 1929; Forest Lookouts dates a tree lookout to the 1910s
September 13, 1930 Roseburg News-Review: a six-foot platform in a fir tree, 71 feet up, reached by a pole ladder, with a small shelter cabin
40-foot round fir pole tower with 14x14 L-4 cab. A September 14, 1933 Roseburg Chieftain item said the CCC would build the lookout before snow fell
Lookout manned 75 days; reporting station at Steamboat Bridge Ranger Station

May 3, 1947: two fliers whose small plane came down about 1,500 feet from the summit reached the unoccupied lookout, broke in and rested two days, then walked about 30 miles to Steamboat guard station
Register: 41-foot treated timber R-6 tower replaced the 1933 tower in 1955. Cinnamon Butte NHLR: first erected on Buster Butte in 1955. Conflicts with the 1962 News-Review date
June 24, 1959 News-Review: a married couple 'will both be on' the lookout for the summer. This is a plan, not a confirmed posting
July 5, 1962 News-Review: a new tower completed about six weeks earlier, replacing the 1933 building, which had become unsafe
Old 1933 building pulled over with cables and a bulldozer winch; debris piled and burned
August 4, 1962 News-Review: a staff member returned for a second stint at the station
41-foot R-6 tower dismantled and moved to Cinnamon Butte, Douglas County; it still stands there and the NHLR says it remains active
Registered November 24, 2010 as US 773, OR 182; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and Cinnamon Butte NHLR say the R-6 tower went up on Buster Butte in 1955; the Forest Service Cinnamon Butte page says built 1955. A July 5, 1962 News-Review item says a new tower was completed about six weeks earlier, replacing the 1933 building. The story reports both and does not choose.
Forest Lookouts dates a tree lookout to the 1910s; the register dates a crow's nest and shelter on the site to 1929. The story uses the 1929 register date and the 1930 newspaper description.

notes_for_editor: Brief access unknown; no summit access source, so no access key. No source describes what remains at the Buster Butte summit today; the register's 2007 photo caption exists but the text does not describe it. Cinnamon Butte tower stands and NHLR says it remains active; its visitor or rental status was not verified, so the story does not claim it. Replacement date conflict (1955 vs 1962) is unresolved. Location references differ across sources (Oakridge, Steamboat, Roseburg). The story uses only the 1941 reporting station (Steamboat Bridge Ranger Station), which the Forest Lookouts page gives directly and which is now evidenced. Brief height 12.2 m matches the 40-foot 1933 tower. Verification 2026-10-09: the story's 1959 married-couple item is a plan from a June 24, 1959 item, not a confirmed posting; the story now says so.
